headline: Auvelity-led growth accelerates, launch spend widens losses
summary_short: Axsome's Q2 2026 revenue rose 45.5% y/y to $218.4M, led by AUVELITY's $180.3M (+51% y/y) on its new Alzheimer's-agitation indication, while the GAAP net loss narrowed q/q to $51.3M (-$0.99/share) from $64.5M in Q1 but widened slightly versus $48.0M a year ago.
summary_long: Growth was broad-based across the three-product portfolio: AUVELITY +51% y/y to $180.3M on its June 2026 Alzheimer's-disease-agitation launch and continued MDD demand; SUNOSI +20% y/y to $35.8M; SYMBRAVO +461% y/y to $2.3M off a small base. SG&A rose to $208.1M from $130.3M y/y on AUVELITY sales-force expansion and SYMBRAVO commercialization, more than offsetting lower R&D ($46.2M vs $49.5M, on reduced AXS-05/AXS-14 spend). SG&A growth outpacing revenue growth widened the operating loss y/y even as it narrowed sequentially off Q1's step-up spend. Cash was $319.9M, down slightly from $322.9M at 2025 year-end. No quantitative guidance was issued; management said current cash is sufficient to fund operations into cash-flow positivity.

drivers.explanation: CEO Herriot Tabuteau cited robust commercial growth driven by strong underlying product demand plus regulatory and clinical pipeline progress (AXS-12 NDA acceptance, FOCUS-2/FOCUS-3 ADHD trial initiations) as the quarter's key themes.

AUVELITY's Alzheimer's-agitation launch (June 2026) plus continued MDD demand drove the largest dollar gain; new-to-brand prescriptions in patients ≥65 rose 126% in the launch's first eight weeks. SUNOSI and SYMBRAVO also grew y/y, the latter off a small prior-year base.
SG&A more than doubled to $208.1M from $130.3M, driven by AUVELITY sales-force expansion for the Alzheimer's launch and SYMBRAVO commercialization, which the release says outpaced revenue growth y/y.
Wider operating loss drove the y/y net-loss widening; the release notes the quarter's net loss includes $27.1 million of stock-based compensation expense.
Per-share loss widened only 2.1% y/y versus net loss's 7.0% widening because diluted share count grew 4.8% y/y, diluting the impact.
